background: Gamini Perera was allotted Lot A depicted in Partition Plan No 2525 dated 2nd February 1981 made by S Silva Licensed Surveyor bearing assessment No 20 Flower Road, Homagama containing in extent 10 perches by a final decree of a partition case bearing No 111/P dated 2nd February 1985 entered in the District Court of Homagama. Gamini Perera by Deed of Deed of Gift No. 515 dated 10th March 1986 attested by R Liyanage Notary Public gifted said Lot A depicted in plan. no 2525 absolutely and irrevocably to his son Suresh Perera subject to life interest of Gamini Perera and his wife Vinitha. Gamini Perera died on 12th June 1990 due to heart failure. Vinitha revoked her life interest over said Lot A depicted in Plan No. 2525 by Deed of revocation of life interest bearing No. 525 dated 25th February 1991 attested by S Sapumal Notary Public. Suresh Perera married Kanthi and had two children namely Rakitha and Muditha. Muditha died due to an accident on 5th June 2023 unmarried and issueless. Rakitha married Ann and died on 2nd July 2022. Suresh Perera died on 10th December 1995 intestate. Suresh Perera had an offspring named Samantha from his first marriage who is a citizen of USA (United States of America).
question: Can Samantha become entitled to the intestate estate of Suresh Perera? Discuss with the provisions of Land (Restriction on alienation) Act No. 38 of 2014 as amended by Land (Restriction on alienation) (Amendment) Act No. 21 of 2018.

background: Sea View Company (Pvt) Ltd wants to purchase a land in Galle facing the sea to construct a hotel. The company was incorporated in Sri Lanka in 2019 and holds a certificate of incorporation numbered PV 00218347. Of its 10,000,000 issued shares, 6,500,000 are held by three Sri Lankan citizens resident in Galle and 3,500,000 are held by Ocean Crest Holdings Pte Ltd, a company incorporated in Singapore. The board has resolved to acquire the property and has authorised its managing director, Ms. Ranmali Fernando, to sign on the company's behalf. The property offered to the company is Lot A depicted in Plan No. 2184 dated 12 January 2021 made by K. A. Wijeratne, Licensed Surveyor, in extent one acre two roods and ten perches, situated at Dadalla within the Galle Municipal Council limits and bounded on the south by the sea. The person offering the land as owner is Mr. D. P. Amarasuriya, who now lives in Melbourne and proposes to sign the transfer through his brother, Mr. L. K. Amarasuriya, acting under a power of attorney granted in Melbourne on 3 March 2024. Mr. D. P. Amarasuriya has produced only Deed of Transfer No. 4712 dated 8 August 2011 attested by S. Perera, Notary Public, and says the earlier deeds in the chain are with his family and can be produced later. A neighbouring family has fenced off and cultivated the northern portion of the land since 2009 and pays nothing to Mr. Amarasuriya. The price agreed between the parties is Rs 100,000,000, and the deed is to be signed at Galle.
question: If you are retained by the said company as their Notary for the said purchase what are the documents you should check prior to purchasing the said land?

background: Herath Mudiyanselage Herath Banda of Thirappane intends to mortgage his land situated in Anuradhapura, which is under the Land Development Ordinance 27 of 1981 amended by the Land Development (Amendment) Act No. 11 of 2022, to a commercial Bank in Sri Lanka for Rupees Ten Million (Rs. 10,000,000/-). The land is Lot 12 in Plan No. 4471 dated 8 June 2012 made by K. Wijeratne, Licensed Surveyor, of the land called Kalugalayaya situated in Thirappane in the Anuradhapura District, in extent two acres. Herath was originally put into occupation of that land on a permit, but he paid the whole of the purchase amount in instalments, developed the land to the satisfaction of the Government Agent, and a grant of the land was issued to him under the said Ordinance on 3 March 2014 and duly registered; he has held under that grant ever since. The intended mortgagee is Ruhunu Commercial Bank PLC, a licensed commercial bank carrying on banking business in Sri Lanka under a licence issued by the Central Bank, and not a registered society. What Herath proposes to mortgage is the whole of the land comprised in the grant, not a divided portion or an undivided share of it, and the mortgage is to be executed on 20 April 2026.
question: Does Herath require approval from the Divisional Secretary to Mortgage the said land?

background: Saman who is a Notary having Notary License to practise in the Judicial Zone of Colombo is employed as a legal officer at a Real estate company in Colombo. Saman's employer instructs him to execute a Deed of Transfer on urgent basis. The transfer concerns Lot 3B depicted in Survey Plan No. 2145 dated 12 March 2019 made by K. B. Ranaweera, Licensed Surveyor, an allotment of land of eighteen perches in extent situated at Talangama North within the Kaduwela Divisional Secretary's Division in the District of Colombo. The intended vendor is Nimal Perera and the intended purchaser is Kamala Silva, a customer of Saman's employer; Saman himself has no interest in the land and is not a party to the transaction. On 19 April 2026 the employer hands Saman a photocopy of Deed of Transfer No. 4512 dated 6 August 2014, by which Nimal Perera says he acquired the land, and tells him to draw and attest the new deed at the company's Colombo office on 20 April 2026 so that the purchase money can be paid the same day. Neither Nimal Perera nor Kamala Silva has given Saman any written authority dispensing with an examination of the land registry, and no extract of the land registry folio for the land has been obtained by anyone.
question: Can Saman execute the said Deed without checking the title at the land registry? Explain with the provisions in Notaries Ordinance.

background:
Saman, who is a Notary having a Notary License to practise in the Judicial Zone of Colombo, is employed as a legal officer at a real estate company in Colombo. His warrant authorises him to practise in the Sinhala language, and his notarial office, where he keeps his records, is at No. 25, Hulftsdorp Street, Colombo 12.

Saman's employer, Sethsiri Realty (Private) Limited of No. 140, Ward Place, Colombo 07, has agreed to buy an allotment of land from Mr. Nimal Perera. The company instructs Saman to execute a Deed of Transfer on an urgent basis. Saman is not a party to the deed, holds no shares in the company and is not one of its directors.

The said land is situated in Kurunegala. It is the allotment called "Kurunduwatta", 0.2023 hectares in extent, at Malkaduwawa village in the Kurunegala Divisional Secretary's Division of the Kurunegala District. Before drawing the deed Saman obtained Mr. Perera's title deed and a certified extract of the relevant folio from the Kurunegala Land Registry, and he intends to tender the completed deed for registration at that registry.

The draft deed is written in Sinhala. Saman proposes that Mr. Perera and the company's authorised signatory sign it before two witnesses on 20 April 2026 at his Hulftsdorp office in Colombo, and that he attest it there.
question: Can Saman attest the said Deed? Explain.

background: Kamal Perera is in occupation in a land situated in Homagama since 1980 by long and prescriptive rights. He wants to get a title certificate to his land under the Registration of Title Act No. 21 of 1998. Kamal Perera retained Sureka Pathirana as his Notary. The land is Lot 42 depicted in Cadastral Map No. HG/1247 prepared by the Surveyor-General for the Homagama title registration area. A title register for that area is kept by the Registrar of Title at the Homagama Title Registry, and the cadastral map used for registration of title in the area is held by the Superintendent of Surveys for the Colombo District. Sureka wishes to attend at the Homagama Title Registry during office hours to examine the folio relating to Lot 42 and to examine the cadastral map, and she also wants to place on her file a certified extract of the folio and a certified copy of an extract of the cadastral map. She is willing to apply on whatever forms are prescribed and to pay whatever fees are prescribed. Kamal has given her no written authority or power of attorney to act for him in the matter, and Sureka is not herself a claimant to Lot 42.
question: Could Sureka inspect the title register and cadastral map on behalf of Kamal? Can she get certified copies of the said documents?

background: Martin Perera wants to dispose his house after his death to Siripala who is his helper by a Last Will and appoints his driver Nihal as the executor of the said Last Will. He does not dispose anything to his children by the said Will. Martin Perera is seventy-two years old, of sound mind and under no legal disability. He is a low-country Sinhalese Buddhist who has lived all his life in Nugegoda within the Colombo district, and he is not governed by Kandyan law, by Thesawalamai or by Muslim law. His wife died in 2018 and he has not remarried. The house is the two-storey dwelling at No. 47/3, Temple Lane, Nugegoda, standing on Lot A in Plan No. 2214, which he bought in 2009 and holds as sole owner on a notarially attested transfer deed; it is his only immovable property and is worth about Rs. 28 million. Siripala Gunasekara, aged forty-five, has worked as Martin's live-in domestic helper for twenty years and is not related to him. Martin's children are two adults, Anusha aged forty and Dinesh aged thirty-seven, both in employment, neither a minor nor dependent on him. Martin has told his lawyer that he does not wish to put into the will any explanation of why he is leaving his children nothing. He proposes to sign the will and to place his thumb impression at the end of it before a notary public and two witnesses, both of them neighbours who take no benefit under the will and neither of whom is married to anyone who does.
question: Can Martin Perera execute the said Will without assigning any reason? Discuss with provisions.

background: Martin Perera wants to dispose his house after his death to Siripala who is his helper by a Last Will and appoints his driver Nihal as the executor of the said Last Will. He does not dispose anything to his children by the said Will. Martin executed that last will on 20 August 2024 at his home at No. 47/3, Temple Lane, Nugegoda, in the Colombo district, signing it and placing his thumb impression at the end before a notary public and two witnesses who were present together; the will was numbered 812 in the notary's protocol and Martin kept the original in a steel safe in his bedroom. He died at that house on 14 February 2026. He left the house at No. 47/3, standing on Lot A in Plan No. 2214 and worth about Rs. 28 million, as his only immovable property, together with about Rs. 1.2 million in a savings account, and he owed a hospital bill of about Rs. 350,000 as well as the funeral expenses. Nihal Silva, aged fifty-two, who had been Martin's driver for eleven years and who lives at Pita Kotte in the same district, opened the safe on 17 February 2026 and found the original will there; he is willing to act as executor. Siripala Gunasekara, the helper named in the will, and Martin's two adult children, Anusha and Dinesh, all survive Martin.
question: After the death of Martin Perera, what steps need to be taken by Nihal?

background: Wimala Gunasekara is a citizen of Sri Lanka who holds a Sri Lankan passport and has lived and worked in Melbourne, Australia for the past nine years. She has agreed to buy from Nihal Weerakoon an allotment of land called Kahatagahawatta, in extent eighteen decimal five perches, situated at Dangedara in the Municipal Council limits of Galle, in the District of Galle, bounded on the North by Lot 3 in Plan No. 2114, on the East by the property of D. Somapala, on the South by Dangedara Road and on the West by a drain, the whole of which was last registered in Volume 214 Folio 85 of the Galle Land Registry. The agreed price is Rs. 14,500,000, and the parties have fixed the first week of December 2025 for the execution of the deed. Wimala's employment contract does not allow her to take leave before March 2026, so she cannot be in Sri Lanka on the execution date. Her brother, Sunil Gunasekara, who lives at Dangedara, Galle, is willing to act for her. On 12 November 2025 Wimala proposes to sign, at the Sri Lanka High Commission in Canberra and before a consular officer there, a written instrument appointing Sunil to act for her in the purchase. She has asked a notary practising in Galle what she must do so that the deed she cannot sign will still be good in law.
question: Advise Wimala according to the latest amendments relating to the Prevention of frauds Ordinance No 7 of 1840.

background: Romani, aged forty-one, is the sole owner of a fifteen-perch allotment of land with a two-storey house standing on it at No. 47/3, Pahalawela Road, Battaramulla, being Lot 12B in Plan No. 3126 dated 8 January 2016 made by K. Amarasiri, Licensed Surveyor. She bought the land from her uncle on Deed of Transfer No. 4821 dated 12 March 2016, attested by W. D. Silva, Notary Public of Colombo, and that deed is registered in Volume/Folio B 218/94 at the Delkanda-Nugegoda Land Registry. She holds the original deed and has obtained a certified copy of the folio; her attorney-at-law is willing to give a written certificate confirming her ownership, and she is ready to swear an affidavit and to lodge her papers in duplicate. Romani leaves for New Zealand on 20 November 2025 to work there for about three years, and no relative will be living in the house; she is afraid that someone may present a forged transfer of the land for registration while she is away. She has given her sister's address at No. 12, Kalapaluwawa Road, Rajagiriya as an address in Sri Lanka at which any notices about her land may be served on her. Before she leaves she also proposes to execute a power of attorney in favour of her brother Nihal, to be registered with the Registrar-General, so that he can act for her in matters concerning the land. Romani, who intends to go to New Zealand, wants to file a caveat to her property situated in Battaramulla and meets you who are a Notary practising in Colombo.
question: Can Romani file a caveat to her property? Who can file a caveat under the Registration of Documents Ordinance which is amended?

background:
Romani, who intends to go to New Zealand, wants to file a caveat to her property situated in Battaramulla and meets you who are a Notary practising in Colombo. The property is an allotment of land of eighteen perches called Kahatagahawatta, at No. 42/7, Pelawatta Road, Battaramulla, registered in Volume 214 Folio 88 of the Battaramulla Land Registry, which Romani bought on a deed of transfer that she has not yet been able to have registered.

Acting on your advice Romani presents a caveat for registration on 3 March 2025, describing that land and giving her Colombo address as the address at which notices are to be served on her, and the Registrar acknowledges receipt and registers it. Romani leaves for New Zealand shortly afterwards.

While the caveat is in force Romani is notified by the Registrar of Lands that a document affecting the land is presented for registration. The document is a deed of transfer of the same allotment of land, executed by a person other than Romani in favour of a purchaser. The Registrar posts the notice to Romani by registered letter to the Colombo address given in her caveat on 12 June 2025.
question: Within how many days has an action to be commenced by Romani?

background: Sunil Bandara Weerakoon, who was born on 14 March 2005 and is therefore 20 years old, lives at No. 27/3, Temple Lane, Nugegoda. He is suffering from a non-curable chronic disease and intends to execute a Last Will. He is unmarried and has no children. His treating consultant physician recorded on 2 September 2025 that although his physical condition is deteriorating he remains fully lucid, understands his affairs, and is able to sign his name and to place a thumb impression without assistance. Sunil wishes to dispose of two assets: a two-storey house standing on the land called Millagahawatta, Lot B in Survey Plan No. 4521 dated 12 June 2018 made by S. Ranaweera, Licensed Surveyor, situated at Pelawatta in the District of Colombo, which came to him under Deed of Gift No. 1120 dated 3 May 2019 from his grandmother; and a fixed deposit of Rs. 2,500,000 held in his own name. He wishes to leave the house to his sister Nayana and the deposit to his mother, and to appoint his uncle Mr. D. B. Weerakoon as executor. He has instructed Mr. K. Perera, a notary public practising in the Colombo District in the Sinhala language, to draw a last will for him alone and not a joint will, and Mr. Perera proposes to attend at Sunil's residence on 20 October 2025 for the execution. The two persons Sunil proposes to have as witnesses are his neighbours Mr. A. Silva and Mrs. R. Fernando, neither of whom, nor either of their spouses, takes any benefit under the intended will.
question: What is the age limit to execute a Last Will according to the latest amendments to the Wills Ordinance? What is the procedure that Sunil should follow? Discuss with relevant provisions in the Ordinance.

background: By a Final Decree dated 22nd October 2001 entered in District Court Kaduwela Partition Case No 2525/P land and premises bearing No 12, Perera Mawatha Battaramulla depicted as Lot 1 in Partition Plan No 1005 dated 24th July 2001 made by H Silva Licensed Surveyor containing in extent 40 perches was allotted to Mahesh Gunesekara. He was married to Malani and had two children namely Kapila and Mithila By Deed of Gift No 925 dated 11th March 2006 attested by PK Hilton Notary Public the said Lot 1 in extent 40 perches was gifted to his son Kapila Gunesekera as an absolute and irrevocable gift subject to life interest of the Donor Mahesh Gunesekara Mahesh Gunesekera died on 24th April 2008. Anusha Gunesekara married to Hasitha Perera and died on 15th June 2012 issueless Prema Gunesekara died on 4th September 2015 unmarried and issueless

background: Kanthi Peiris is a Notary practicing in Colombo. Shantha Ratnayake is her brother-in-law and is the owner of an apartment in Negambo. However, Shantha who lives in Negambo is unable to come to Colombo to sign the Agreement.
question: How can this Agreement be signed by both parties and what steps should Kanthi follow with regard to the registration of this Agreement?

background:
Kanthi Peiris is a Notary practicing in Colombo. Shantha Ratnayake is her brother-in-law and is the owner of an apartment in Negambo. After the execution of the Lease Agreement, the Notary Kanthi Peiris remembered that she could not obtain the Yearly Certificate from the Registrar of High Court for the current year.
question: What are her liabilities in this regard?

background: Mr. Ranasinghe is your client and he intends to buy a coconut estate with a bungalow situated in Kurunegala thirty acres (A30, RO, PO) in extent. He is a citizen of Sri Lanka, resident in Colombo 5, and he owns no other agricultural land. The property is known as Pinnaduwa Watta, depicted as Lot 1 in Survey Plan No. 4127 dated 12 June 2019 made by K. Amarasekara, Licensed Surveyor, and lies in the village of Kadigawa, Wariyapola Divisional Secretary's Division, Dewamedi Hatpattu, Kurunegala District; the whole thirty acres is under mature coconut and carries one two-storeyed bungalow. The intended vendor is Mr. K. B. Wijesundara Bandara of Wariyapola, who says he became owner on Deed of Transfer No. 1032 attested on 4 March 1998 by Mr. S. Herath, Notary Public of Kurunegala, and that the land was allotted to his predecessor by a partition decree entered in 1979 in the District Court of Kurunegala. He holds no state permit or grant in respect of the land, and there is no tea or rubber on it. The vendor has disclosed that the estate stands mortgaged to a licensed commercial bank on Bond No. 2210 dated 8 July 2021, with about Rs. 8,500,000 outstanding. The parties signed an agreement to sell on 10 January 2024 at a price of Rs. 42,000,000, of which Rs. 4,200,000 has been paid as an advance and the balance is to be paid on execution of the conveyance, which they wish to have executed on 20 May 2024. You are authorised to practise in Sinhala in the Kurunegala district and your office is at Kurunegala.
question: If you are retained by him, what steps should you take as the Motary on behalf of Mr. Ranasinghe?

background:
Ceylon Rubber Company (Private) Limited wishes to purchase a Rubber Estate situated in Galle, Forty One Acres (A41, RO, PO) in extent.

The company was incorporated in Sri Lanka on 12 March 2015 under registration number PV 91234. It has five shareholders, each holding twenty per cent of the issued shares. All five are citizens of Sri Lanka resident in Galle, no share is held directly or indirectly by any person or body outside Sri Lanka, and none of the five owns any other land that is used or is capable of being used for agriculture. The company owns no land other than its registered office premises at No. 14, Wackwella Road, Galle. As at its last audited balance sheet dated 31 March 2023 the total value of the company's assets was Rs. 60,000,000, and the price agreed with the vendor for the estate is Rs. 41,000,000. The articles adopted when the company was incorporated contain no provision expressly authorising the acquisition of estate property.

The estate, known as Mahagoda Estate, is planted with mature rubber and is 16.6 hectares in extent. It has never been registered, and is not deemed to be registered, as an estate in the statutory register of rubber estates. The vendor is Mr. D. P. Wickramasinghe, a citizen of Sri Lanka, who says he has held the estate since Deed of Transfer No. 1420 dated 12 June 1998 attested by A. B. Silva, Notary Public of Galle, and that the estate is registered in the Galle Land Registry in volume and folio E 214/86. He has disclosed that a mortgage bond he granted to a commercial bank in 2019 is registered in that folio and has not been discharged, and he has so far produced only a photocopy of his own deed. Your instructions were received on 5 September 2023 and the parties wish to complete in October 2023.
question: If you are retained by the company for the said purchase, what steps should you take?

background:
Ceylon Rubber Company (Private) Limited wishes to purchase a Rubber Estate situated in Galle, Forty One Acres (A41, RO, PO) in extent.

The said Ceylon Rubber Company (Private) Limited instructs you to examine the title of a residential premises situated next to said Rubber Estate, Forty Perches (AO, RO, P40) in extent.

The premises, known as "Nelumwatta" and bearing assessment number 22, Wakwella Road, are Lot A depicted in Plan No. 2456 dated 3 March 1996 made by K. Perera, Licensed Surveyor. They lie within the Akmeemana Divisional Secretary's Division in the District of Galle and adjoin the eastern boundary of the Rubber Estate. A single-storey dwelling house built in about 1998 stands on the land. The parcel has not been brought within any area declared for the purposes of the title registration scheme, so the Galle Land Registry folio remains the only public record of dealings with it.

The vendor is Mrs. S. K. Amarasuriya, a citizen of Sri Lanka, who says she bought the premises on Deed of Transfer No. 3120 dated 8 July 2004 attested by L. Jayasinghe, Notary Public of Galle, and that her predecessors held on a deed of 1985 and a deed of 1972. She has so far produced only a photocopy of the 2004 deed, no earlier deed and no registry extract. She mentions that a loan she took in 2016 was secured on the premises, and that a relative lodged some document at the Land Registry in 2022 objecting to any dealing with the property.

A shed and a well at the southern end of the premises have been occupied since about 2010 by a neighbour, Mr. W. Gunaratne, who claims that strip as his own and pays no rent and renders no service to the vendor. Your firm was instructed on 20 September 2023 and the company wishes to complete before the end of the year.
question: What documents would you call for the examination of the title and why?

background: Wimalasena Perera, aged 74, a retired schoolmaster of Panadura, gifted the land called Kahatagahawatta, thirty-two perches in extent with the house standing on it, at Panadura in the District of Kalutara, to his nephew Chaminda Perera. The parties are low-country Sinhalese governed by the general law. The gift was made by deed No. 4417 dated 12 March 2019, attested by a notary public and registered in the Kalutara land registry, and the deed states that the gift is absolute and irrevocable. The donee took possession, and the donor went on living in an annexe of the same house as the deed allowed him to. In June 2023 the donee assaulted the donor during a quarrel over the property, causing injuries for which the donor was treated in hospital, and then locked the annexe and put the donor out of the premises; the donor has since been living with a daughter. The donee does not deny the assault or the eviction and refuses to reconvey the property. The donor consults you in October 2023 and asks whether he can get the property back.
question: Could it be revoked?

background:
Rohan Perera purchased a house and property in December 1977 for Rs.250,000/-, and done improvements to the house to the value of Rs.800,000/-. The property is presently valued at Rs.6,500,000/-. He wishes to gift the said property to his son Wasantha.

The property is Lot 12 depicted in Plan No. 2456 dated 3 March 1974 made by K. B. Wijesinghe, Licensed Surveyor, in extent fifteen decimal five perches, together with the two storeyed dwelling house bearing Assessment No. 47/3, Pathiragoda Road, Maharagama, within the Divisional Secretary's Division of Maharagama in the District of Colombo, Western Province. Rohan Perera bought it outright and at arm's length from an unrelated seller by Deed of Transfer No. 1187 dated 12 December 1977 attested by S. A. Dissanayake, Notary Public, and the Rs.250,000/- he paid was the open market price of the land and house on that date. The improvements costing Rs.800,000/- were an additional upper floor, a garage and a boundary wall, all built between 1996 and 1999, that is after he bought the property and before the deed he now proposes. He is the sole owner, the property is free of any mortgage or lease, and he intends an outright gift, keeping no life interest or other reservation for himself or anyone else. The Deed of Gift in favour of his son Wasantha Perera is to be executed at Colombo on 14 October 2022, and a valuation report dated 1 October 2022 by a chartered valuer puts the open market price of the property on that date at Rs.6,500,000/-.
question: What is the value you would mention in the Deed of Gift for stamp duty purpose?

background: Nimal, a retired schoolteacher of Pelawatta, has been in possession of a land registered under Registration of Title Act for more than 10 years. The land is Land Parcel No. 214 delineated on Cadastral Map No. 520150 for the village of Pelawatta in the Homagama Divisional Secretary's Division, an area the Minister declared by Order published in the Gazette to be an area to which the Registration of Title Act applies. The Title Register for that parcel records Somapala as the registered owner, registered with a First Class Title of Absolute Ownership on 3 March 2009. Saman failed to comply with rules set out in section 31 of the Notaries Ordinance when attesting the said Deed. Nimal Perera signed the deed at that office in Saman's presence and in the presence of one attesting witness, Kamala Silva, who also signed there. background:

background: Anura Perera your client wants to purchase a house and property situated in Rajagiriya said to be belonging to one Kusum Peiris and gives you a copy of a Transfer Deed No. 234 dated 23rd March, 2015 attested by Walter de Silva Notary Public and a copy of a Survey Plan No.1125 dated 2nd January, 2000 made by Anil Silva Licensed Surveyor relating to an allotment of land marked Lot B together with a Reservation for a Road marked Lot R of the Land called Dewatagahawatta in extent of 30 perches situated in Rajagiriya. background:

background: The Notary knows the testator who wishes to execute a last Will and who is sick and taking treatment warded in a hospital.
